name: Hedylus
bio: Hedylus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 3rd century BC. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book V: 199; Book VI: 292).

poems.title: Book V, 199
poems.author: Hedylus
poems.text: Wine and treacherous toasts and the sweet love of Nicagoras sent Aglaonicé to sleep; and here hath she dedicated to Cypris these spoils of her maiden love still all dripping with scent, her sandals and the soft band that held her bosom, witnesses to her sleep and his violence then.

poems.title: Book VI, 292
poems.author: Hedylus
poems.text: The snood and purple vest, and the Laconian robes, and the gold piping for the tunic, all fell to () Niconoe, for the girl was an ambrosial blossom of the Loves and Graces. ‘Therefore to Priapus, who was judge in the beauty-contest, she dedicates the fawn-skin and this golden jug.

poems.title: Book XI, 123
poems.author: Hedylus
poems.text: Aais neither purged Aristagoras, nor touched him, but no sooner had he come in than Aristagoras was gone. What aconite has such natural virtue? Ye coffin-makers, throw chaplets and garlands on Agis.

poems.title: Book XI, 414
poems.author: Hedylus
poems.text: The daughter of limb-relaxing Bacchus and limb-relaxing Aphrodite is limb-relaxing Gout.
